title: Network pharmacology-based investigation on the mechanism of aloin in ameliorating atherosclerosis by regulating macrophage polarization.
authors: Tian, Ye; Mei, Xianghui; Zeng, Fang; Li, Baichao; Du, Wentao; Chen, Xianru
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究芦荟素通过NF-kB/STAT3通路调控巨噬细胞极化改善动脉粥样硬化，核心是药物-蛋白作用，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，也无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory vascular disease in which macrophage polarization plays a pivotal role in plaque progression and stability. Aloin, a major anthraquinone compound isolated from Aloe vera, possesses potent anti-inflammatory activities; however, its therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms in AS remain insufficiently understood. In the present study, a network pharmacology approach combined with molecular docking, cellular experiments, and animal validation was employed to investigate the protective effects of aloin against AS and elucidate its molecular mechanism. Common targets shared by aloin, macrophage polarization, and AS were identified, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction and GO/KEGG enrichment analyses. Molecular docking demonstrated strong binding affinities of aloin toward key inflammatory targets, particularly NF-kappaB and STAT3. Experimental validation showed that aloin significantly suppressed nitric oxide production in lipopolysaccharide-induced RAW264.7 macrophages and inhibited M1 macrophage polarization while promoting the M2 phenotype, as evidenced by decreased expression of iNOS and TNF-alpha and increased expression of Arg-1 and IL-10. In ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet, aloin markedly reduced aortic plaque formation and alleviated vascular pathological injury. Mechanistically, both in vitro and in vivo analyses revealed that aloin significantly attenuated the phosphorylation of NF-kappaB and STAT3, thereby blocking activation of the NF-kappaB/STAT3 signaling pathway. Collectively, these findings suggest that aloin may contribute to the amelioration of atherosclerotic lesions by modulating macrophage polarization balance through inhibition of NF-kappaB/STAT3 signaling, highlighting its potential as a candidate worthy of further investigation for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerosis.
abstract_zh: 动脉粥样硬化（AS）是一种慢性炎症性血管疾病，其中巨噬细胞极化在斑块进展和稳定性中发挥关键作用。芦荟苷（Aloin）是从芦荟中分离的主要蒽醌类化合物，具有强效抗炎活性；然而，其在AS中的治疗潜力及潜在机制仍未被充分理解。本研究采用网络药理学方法，结合分子对接、细胞实验和动物验证，探讨芦荟苷对AS的保护作用并阐明其分子机制。鉴定了芦荟苷、巨噬细胞极化和AS共有的靶点，随后进行了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络构建及GO/KEGG富集分析。分子对接显示芦荟苷对关键炎症靶点，特别是NF-kappaB和STAT3，具有强结合亲和力。实验验证表明，芦荟苷显著抑制脂多糖诱导的RAW264.7巨噬细胞中一氧化氮的产生，并抑制M1型巨噬细胞极化，同时促进M2表型，表现为iNOS和TNF-alpha表达降低，Arg-1和IL-10表达升高。在高脂饮食喂养的ApoE-/-小鼠中，芦荟苷显著减少主动脉斑块形成并缓解血管病理损伤。机制上，体外和体内分析均显示，芦荟苷显著减弱NF-kappaB和STAT3的磷酸化，从而阻断NF-kappaB/STAT3信号通路的激活。综合这些发现表明，芦荟苷可能通过抑制NF-kappaB/STAT3信号通路调节巨噬细胞极化平衡，从而有助于改善动脉粥样硬化病变，凸显其作为动脉粥样硬化预防和治疗候选药物的潜力，值得进一步研究。
